title: ISO 42001 Annex A Control A.5 – Assessing Impacts of AI Systems
description: Annex A Control A.5 addresses the assessment of AI systems’ impacts, focusing on evaluating potential consequences to individuals, groups, and societies throughout the AI system’s lifecycle. It emphasises establishing a formal process for impact assessment, ensuring comprehensive documentation and consideration of AI system impacts on societal and individual levels.

subtitle: What Is Annex A Control A.5 – Assessing Impacts of AI Systems
content: Control A.5 ensures organisations assess AI impacts across their lifecycle, promoting ethical, transparent, and responsible AI use.

subsections.heading: Critical Nature of Impact Assessment for Compliance
subsections.content: Impact assessments aren’t just regulatory—they’re essential to identify and mitigate negative consequences on individuals, groups, and society, ensuring respect for human rights.

subsections.heading: Contribution to Ethical AI Management
subsections.content: By mandating thorough impact evaluations (fairness, accountability, transparency, bias mitigation), Control A.5 demonstrates an organisation’s commitment to responsible AI.

title: The AI System Impact Assessment Process

subsections.heading: Steps Required to Establish a Comprehensive AI Impact Assessment Process
list: Identify Triggers: When an impact assessment is necessary.
Define Assessment Elements: What to measure, how to analyze consequences and likelihood.
Assign Responsibilities: Who performs the assessment.
Utilise the Assessment: How results inform system design, triggering reviews.

subsections.heading: Ensuring a Thorough and Effective Assessment Process
list: Incorporate Diverse Perspectives: Engage experts, users, impacted individuals.
Adopt Continuous Improvement: Regularly update assessments with new insights.

subsections.heading: Addressing Potential Consequences for Individuals and Societies
list: Evaluate impacts on legal positions, wellbeing, human rights, societal norms.
Consider protection needs of vulnerable groups (children, elderly, workers).

title: Documentation of AI System Impact Assessments

subsections.heading: Requirements for Documenting AI System Impact Assessments
subsections.content: Meticulously document intended use, misuse scenarios, identified impacts, mitigation measures, affected demographics, system complexity, and human oversight roles.

subsections.heading: Importance of Retaining Assessment Results
subsections.content: Retention supports compliance, transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement through auditability.

subsections.heading: Determining the Retention Duration
subsections.content: Balance legal requirements, policy needs, and system characteristics—often exceeding minimum periods for robust risk management.

title: Assessing AI System Impact on Individuals or Groups – A.5.4

subsections.heading: Considerations for Assessing AI’s Impact on Individuals
subsections.content: Evaluate effects on legal rights, life opportunities, physical/psychological wellbeing, human rights, societal norms—direct and indirect.

subsections.heading: Ensuring Inclusive Assessments
list: Engage diverse stakeholders including vulnerable groups.
Apply guidelines for children, elderly, individuals with disabilities.

subsections.heading: The Role of Human Oversight
list: Implement human intervention mechanisms in AI operations.
Define clear accountability structures for oversight.

subsections.heading: Structuring Assessments for Fairness, Accountability, Transparency
list: Promote transparency with clear criteria and processes.

subsections.heading: Understanding Societal Impact
subsections.content: Broad effects on environment, economy, governance, health, culture—both positive (access, efficiency) and negative (inequality).

subsections.heading: Approaches to Assessing Societal Impacts
list: Conduct comprehensive reviews of environmental, economic, and social effects.
Engage stakeholders (community reps, experts) for societal insights.

subsections.heading: AI’s Influence on Sustainability & Economy
subsections.content: Optimises resources, can reduce waste, but may increase energy use and economic disparities.
